status: registered before tile selection, patch-2 extraction, new AlphaEarth downloads or scoring; A1 (MS-163) results are known
scenario: docs/SCENARIO_RAPID_CHANGE_20260927.md — D+3 after a disaster, no labels, hazard unknown: which areas changed?
question: Does the full label-free tool (per-acquisition OlmoEarth embeddings + normalisation by the location's own pre-event variability + evidence-guided 20 m zoom) beat the strongest of AlphaEarth and the classic SAR index (each in raw and normalised form) on BOTH tile detection and localisation, across all KuroSiwo flood events since 2019?
data: KuroSiwo, all splits (label-free, no training), flood year >= 2019; per event <= 80 flood tiles, all permanent-water-only tiles, dry = max(#flood, 10); deterministic hash selection (code/a1b_scenario_v0.py select)

methods.full_method: T1: olmo4_norm tile mean; T2: olmo_adapt (olmo2_norm for the top 30% tiles by olmo4_norm tile score, olmo4_norm upsampled elsewhere)
methods.eps: median of each method's own pre-event change over all selected tiles (label-free constant)
methods.patch2: code/a1b_extract_s1_change_v0.py: identical preprocessing to the S1 cache, patch 2 (20 m tokens), change maps only

metrics.T1: tile AUC flood vs dry+perm (primary), flood vs perm (secondary)
metrics.T2: token AUC at a common 20 m grid, tokens with flood fraction >= .5 vs 0 inside flood tiles
metrics.ci: event-clustered bootstrap (2000) of full - strongest baseline

strongest_baseline: per metric, the best of the four baselines on the evaluation set itself (conservative: favours the baselines)

verdict.meaningful: full - strongest >= 0.05 with CI lower > 0 on BOTH T1 (flood vs dry+perm) and T2

compute_reporting: per-tile GPU seconds for patch 2 vs patch 4 extraction (patch 4 timed on a subset), fraction of tiles zoomed
not_claimed: comparison with Google Custom Satellite Embeddings (not accessible)
